# DSPy

> DSPy is a framework for programming—rather than prompting—language models. Instead of hand-tuning prompt strings, you write compositional Python: declarative Signatures describe input/output behavior, Modules implement strategies for satisfying them, and optimizers (teleprompters) tune prompts and weights against metrics you define.

This file indexes the source repository for AI agents. For the rendered documentation index, see https://dspy.ai/llms.txt.

## Core concepts

- [Signatures](dspy/signatures/): declarative input/output specs; `Signature`, `InputField`, `OutputField`, and string-signature parsing in `dspy/signatures/signature.py`
- [Modules and prediction](dspy/predict/): `Predict`, `ChainOfThought`, `ReAct`, and other strategies built on signatures
- [Primitives](dspy/primitives/): `Module` base class, `Example`, `Prediction`, and the Python interpreter tool
- [Adapters](dspy/adapters/): translate between signatures and LM message formats (chat, JSON, XML, two-step)
- [LM clients](dspy/clients/): `dspy.LM` and provider integrations built on LiteLLM, plus caching and fine-tuning jobs
- [Optimizers](dspy/teleprompt/): prompt/weight optimization, e.g. `BootstrapFewShot`, `MIPROv2`, `GEPA`

## Key reference points

- [Exception taxonomy](dspy/utils/exceptions.py): `DSPyError` and its subclasses
- [Settings and context rules](dspy/dsp/utils/settings.py): global configuration, thread ownership, and `dspy.context` overrides
- [Callback system](dspy/utils/callback.py): `BaseCallback` hooks around modules, LMs, adapters, and tools

## Docs

- [DSPy documentation](https://dspy.ai)
- [Docs index for LLMs](https://dspy.ai/llms.txt)

## Development

- Run tests: `uv run pytest tests/`
- Lint: `uv run ruff check .`
